steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Hey, lad. Whatever you need, just spill it.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: You're scaring all my customers away with your grim face. I can't do business like this.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Yeah?

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Lad, how about I show you the flowers that have just arrived?

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Are you getting flowers for your mum or your crush at school?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: N... Neither.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I saw your recruitment poster.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Do you wish to work here?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: If you need help...

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: You're an Infected?

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I can't hire you.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...It's fine. You're not the only one who's turned me away.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I'm sorry for taking up your time.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Hey, hold on a sec.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Why do you want this job?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...I like plants.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: That's a decent reason.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: I like plants too because they know how to play to their strengths.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: They can neither talk nor move, but their appeal lies in their colorful flowers and pleasant scents.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Many plants don't flower and have no scent...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: They deserve our love too, right?

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: You're interesting, lad. Hmm.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: I do have a job in mind that might be suitable for you.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Won't be too much human contact, just need to get your hands dirty working with flowers and plants. And it requires you to go dangerous places on the regular.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: I know this supplier who's on the hunt for plant hunters. Simply put, he needs someone to help him collect rare plants.

steps.name: Florist
steps.text: Wanna give it a shot?

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Whoaagh—

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: I-Is this a...

steps.name: Flustered Mobber & Composed Mobber
steps.text: Trap?!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Who are you lot?

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: What, us? Whuhh...

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: ...We're tourists.

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Yeah, that, we're tourists!

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: We heard that this old abandoned manor had some smashing scenery, so we came by for a stroll!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: For real?

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: For real...

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: Something cold is touching me...

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: I feel it too... What is this...

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Vines?! Why are they moving?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Many have set their sights on this manor lately. You'd better come clean and tell me why you're here.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Or I'll feed you to these carnivorous plants like those who came before you.

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: And who are you...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: You're asking me?

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Stop wasting your breath with him! Just tell him the truth! I can't stand these bloody vines around my neck!

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: ...We're here looking for thornblooms.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Oh? Thornbloom, is it.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: There's not even a single bud here in this manor, let alone thornblooms.

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: It's right there under that sculpture! I swear on my granny's life!

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Thornbloom is the root of the plant! Just dig it up and you'll see how it got its name.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Turns out it was those weeds...

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: Is he off looking for thornblooms? Could he be a plant hunter too...

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: You sodding idiot, look how soft these vines are. They can't choke you.

steps.name: Flustered Mobber
steps.text: ...Did he bluff me?!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Thornbloom...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: The roots do look like a flower. Thorny and henna-colored.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: According to my boss, its price's gone through the roof in the black market... thanks to its very high medicinal value.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It doesn't flower and has no scent, but its roots can cure sickness, so people need it.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: They even give it a flower name when it doesn't flower.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Ugh—
Just as Verdant bends down to pick the thornbloom, he notices a solitary tuft of grass growing beside it.
It's nothing remarkable, but here in this wheat field, it sticks out like a sore thumb.
When the wind blows, the unripe wheat plants all bend to one side.
At that instant, the tuft of grass finally reveals itself to the sun.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: What have we here...
Verdant sees the grass and notices his hand that has reached for the valuable thornbloom.
If it weren't for the gust of wind, he probably never would've found this tuft of grass.
All of a sudden, he feels somewhat ashamed.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: Hey, kid.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: Which village are you from?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: (Wary) What's your business?

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: What's your business? You have the face to ask that when you're wandering about my land looking suspicious.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: How dare you glare at me, huh? Get yourself out of my field. I'm weeding.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Weeding?
Upon hearing that, Verdant instinctively glances at the unknown grass behind him.
Knowing he will sound weird and annoying, he speaks anyway...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I'm staying put.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: You brat!
Verdant!

steps.name: Surprised Man
steps.text: God, it IS you... Verdant, mate, how long's it been?

steps.name: Surprised Man
steps.text: Oi, Uncle Watson, the scythe doesn't go that high, come on, you could poke someone's...oh, were you having arow?

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: You know this boy, Tucker?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Of course! We're classmates!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Were classmates.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Not anymore now.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Haha, you haven't changed one bit.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Uncle Watson, you don't get this pissed off, do you... Could be it's just a misunderstanding?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: My classma— Verdant here might come off as a bit intimidating, and he's not good at dealing with strangers. But really, he means no harm.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: Okay, then maybe you can talk some sense into him and let him know he's not only a nuisance but also rude.

steps.name: Farmer
steps.text: Hurry up and get him off my land! If I go on arguing with him, I'll be too knackered to bicker with my ball and chain tonight!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Come in and have a seat. No one's home, so you can relax.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Sure.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I just realized you're a local here.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Wait, what? Just half a minute ago I thought you came all the way here to hang out with me.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Fine. You wouldn't have argued with a farmer over some weeds if you were here to visit me.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Thanks for helping me out just now.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: No big deal... Of course, I'd love some help with my fieldwork report if you're up for it.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I think I'll sit this one out. I don't want to...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: No, mate, it's fine. I actually didn't think you would say yes. It was just a joke.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Hey...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: I thought you weren't in your right mind trying to save that weed from him.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Now, it sits beautifully in your specimen box.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker, I don't think it's just a weed.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Eh? Isn't this just a millet or some other wild grass... Forget it. As someone who failed the course, I shouldn't argue with one of the top three.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I'm not saying it isn't...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Hello? Why are you frozen...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...It sort of resembles a millet, but it isn't one. I just noticed it.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Look here. Seems like it'd have the same conical kind of inflorescence as bristlegrass, right?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: And the stalk is a bit sedge-like...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: So, it's an undiscovered species?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Can only say I've never seen it. Don't remember reading about it in any books either.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: A new species? That's possible.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Can't believe you crossed a farmer holding a scythe for it when you hadn't the slightest clue what it was. That's not the Verdant I know!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I don't know why I did it either... I just felt like I had to protect it.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Maybe you did the right thing. What if it IS a new species?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Hah, I was right.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: This is exactly why I wanted your help with my field report!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: You have an eye to tell what's distinctive about the most unremarkable of plants. That's what separates me apart from a top student...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I almost overlooked it too, actually.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It has no economic value. It's not something a plant hunter needs.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: And so what? What matters is you were sharp enough to find it.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...I've got an idea. If we want to know if it's a new species, we can send it to a botanical institute or something for identification.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Identification? Alright... But before that, I've still got work to do.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Got to head back to base.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Yeah, I got the thornbloom. Harvested the full plant intact, and collected a sample of the soil it was growing in too.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Competitors? I think I ran across two... No, they didn't get in my way. It was the other way round, actually...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Other plants of economic value...? No, nothing in particular.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I've sent you the data and photos. If everything's good, I'll be on my way back tomorrow.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: There's a new commission, you said?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: How about I go back and confirm the target with you in person before heading out again?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Even though it's urgent, I... No, I'm not doubting your judgment. I trust you, but I—

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Alright, I understand.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I'll head back the moment I've got the new target plant. Is that alright?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: So, no chance of hitting the institutes?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Your boss... sounds like a real pain with the way he talks. Can't you just go back and tell him you didn't find the thing he wanted?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Not unless I don't want this job...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Too bad then.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Being a plant hunter is so much cooler than being stuck in a lab rinsing test tubes and sticking labels on specimens all day! If I were you, I wouldn't trade the job for the world!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: How about this—you don't have to help with my field report if you can take me along plant-hunting once! Pretty please!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Haha.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Sneaking into the target area by following a meticulous plan, fooling the eyes of all, and avoiding danger until reaching the 'final chamber' where the target object lies...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Have you watched that Wrankwood movie that came out last month, the adventure one? The protagonist was hunted down by the natives while looking for treasure in the Sargonian rainforest? That's basically you!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I—No, I haven't watched...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Thought so.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker, you know I don't really care about those things... I don't work as a plant hunter because I'm into adventures, either.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I do it because I need a livelihood, and I enjoy working with plants.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It's the best opportunity I've had since catching Oripathy.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...Good for you, Verdant.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: I got you. It was the school's mistake to make you drop out because of Oripathy. They've lost a young scholar with a real passion for plants.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: If the professor knew you took on such a risky job just to keep studying plants, he'd definitely regret not pleading your case to the school back then!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Heh... Should I blame him?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker, still remember how we used to cultivate those specimens before?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...Aren't you still pretty good at it?
As he speaks, Verdant closes the lid of the thornbloom's incubator and opens up another specimen case, which is smaller and warmer.
He feels the moisture of the soil within using his fingertip. Then, he gives the glass walls of the case a spritz from his spray bottle.
The nameless grass makes no sound, but he knows it's growing.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Honestly speaking, you looked like a changed man when you were tending to the plants.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Maybe it's because I don't have to worry about them rejecting me.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Reject? Maybe... But as you know, plants don't always act the way we want either.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Just like those specimens we had in the greenhouse back then. Some barely grew, and some withered early on...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...And don't forget the ones that had us going until they started blooming and bearing, just to show us they weren't even the right ones.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: So, you might want to keep your expectations low...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Expectations?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Are you worried that I might be devastated if that grass turns out to be just an ordinary weed?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Mmm.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I won't. I don't look after it for the elusive possibility of it becoming something extraordinary.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker, if you saw it growing next to the crops, what would you do?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: I'd pull it out, of course. It doesn't even fit to be used as compost...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Right... That was what I used to think for a long time.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: But at that time, I thought I was someone important, like the crop. I never imagined one day I'd have nowhere left to go.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Now, I'm even more useless than compost... At least, compost can still be kept on the field.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Verdant...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It's alright, Tucker. I'm doing pretty well now, right?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I've thought it through—I don't really expect it to be a new species.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I just think that... it deserves a little place of its own.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: When you think about it, you'll realize that it hardly needs anything at all.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Soil, water, and sunlight... That's it. Enough to sustain its growth.
Verdant suddenly feels an urge to ask the nameless grass some questions.
What's your name?
Do you long to be noticed?
Are... Are you scared of being rejected too?
Little grass...
...You'd much rather go back to the vast field than be stuck in a little specimen case, right?
'...You'd better go. Now.'
'Get out of here!'
It's...
'You saw it too. It was a unanimous decision by the school board.'
'You should prioritize your health over learning here, right?'
'...True, they're not contradictory, but we have to consider the welfare of the students and staff here.'
'That's out of the question. The school would never let you have a whole dorm room just to yourself.'
Alright. I'll leave, then.
'College graduate? We just need someone who can bring in customers... You're an Infected? Well, that won't do.'
'We don't hire the Infected as typists. Oh, you can work from home? You promise your efficiency won't be affected? Dream on!'
'Hey, you, keep away from my shop! Don't let me catch you around here again! The quarantine, that's where you belong!'
'Sorry, we can't hire you.'
Alright. I'll leave, then.
'All these straw hats and sandals. You haven't sold a single one?'
'Trust me, I've asked around! No buyers are willing to take them! Tsk... Even the village head is avoiding us now.'
'Maybe we can try at a nomadic city next...'
'That's quite a good idea, actually. I'll head to the market tomorrow and bring with me the premium cotton cloth Mother left behind. Maybe we can get a second-hand cart with it!'
'And take my silver bracelet too! There has to be a way... We have to let him stay. No matter what, he's still our son...'
Maybe I should go. Even if there's no turning back to my old life, I have to pull myself together.
But... where can I go?
Huh?
...God, what a racket.
Fine, I'll go. Stop trying to kick me out! I can survive without you!
'Verdant—'
I know what to do! Just shut up!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Was it a dream...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: The grass... is still there.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Eh? There seems to be a new bud sprouting here.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I know some plants will experience a growth spurt when they sense a drastic change in their environment.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Little grass, do you feel safe inside this specimen case?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Hey, Verdant!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Open up! Don't tell me you're still sleeping!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker? Why are you here?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...WHY AM I HERE?!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Oh, please. Didn't you promise to take me to experience plant hunting yesterday?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Wasn't that a joke?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Let's move! Many hands make light work!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: We can hit the botanical institute sooner too, right?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Can't believe you're still thinking about that... It doesn't harm to do the identification, I guess.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Fine, let's do this together.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: You aren't helping by leaving your footprints everywhere we've passed by.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Yahoo—

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: How's that? I can easily jump to the other roof—whoawhoawhoaaahh ohgodhelpmeMum!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Careful!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Phew, that was close. Luckily, it was the tile that fell and not me.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Thanks for catching me, Verdant...? Wait, why is the 'Scarecrow' here?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Unlike you, I'll climb up from the ground.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Don't need to thank the 'Scarecrow'. It probably just didn't want you to cause a ruckus that would alert all the villagers.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Nice work! That's the Verdant I know from school.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: You are a working adult now. Can't you be more tolerant of your friend? How immature!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: No dilly-dallying, Tucker. Jump in through that chimney.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: What? The chimney?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Wait, shouldn't we knock before going in? Waitwaitwaitwait, why is your 'Scarecrow's' pushing me—
Total silence.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Well?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: The 'Scarecrow' caught me. I guess it was a safe landing?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...I didn't scream out loud. That took me a lot of effort, you know!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Good for you. Coming down.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Phew... Can you hear it? My heart's pounding like a sledgehammer!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Can't believe I just reached the 'final chamber' with a plant hunter and had my hands on a 'mysterious ancient seed'!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: We just took the target object from an empty hut... Don't exaggerate things.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Well, this isn't as exciting as I imagined it would be!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: I mean, where was the sleuthing part? We went in, we grabbed it, we got out... Is that it? Way too easy!

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: This seed doesn't look rare either...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I think it was left here by the previous agent.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Agent?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Plant hunters don't just handle dangerous missinos There's simple work like this too, which involves collecting an object at a designated location.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...Like a Messenger?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I heard the very first batch of plant hunters were Messengers specializing in international spice trade.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Being a plant hunter doesn't sound cool anymore...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Time to head back to base. I need to debrief with my boss. I hope he won't give me any more assignments.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Tucker, I reminded you to clean your shoes after we stepped through the mud.

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Eh? I did. Look, they are as clean as a whistle.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Then, whose footprints are these... Why do they look so similar to the ones near the base?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Can't be...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Eh? Excuse me? Why are you running—

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Move! We're running out of time!
From a distance, Verdant spots thick smoke rising from the base.
With all the strength he has, he sprints. The pungent smell of the smoke makes it hard for him to breathe.
The uneasy feelings before have taken form in the fire before his eyes.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Delighted Mobber
steps.text: Well, look what he's brought us... A surprise!

steps.name: Delighted Mobber
steps.text: We've got a packet of square sunflower seeds here! That'll make us a pretty penny!

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: Enough. Shut it.

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: Damage all the emergency communicators in the base. Take whatever's useful.

steps.name: Composed Mobber
steps.text: We must get out of here before he wakes up.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Don't...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Why...
Mum, should we clear the weeds in the field?
'Yes. They'll impede the growth of the crops.'
Can we just move them away from the crops? Like, our courtyard?
I want to know what they look like when they grow up.
'Hmm... Good idea.'
'They might grow into wheat, or maybe corn.'
'I hear a very long time ago, weeds were no different from the grains.'
...What if we can't eat them?
What if they grow ugly flowers and turn really smelly? That'd be awful!
'Haha! Have you become old enough to be bothered by these things? Don't worry—'
'They'll still have their own worth.'

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Verdant! Were the two guys that ran off holding the thormbloom incubator?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: ...Are you injured?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Little...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: Should I go after them?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Check on... the grass...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: T—The grass? Please tell me you won't go inside...

steps.name: Tucker
steps.text: No! The fire's getting out of control! Don't go in, Verdant!

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: That grass... I still haven't taken it to the institute...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I still haven't given it a name...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It survived in the field even when nobody tended to it...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It shouldn't be pulled out or be devoured by flames...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It shouldn't be chased away or forgotten...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: It is just trying to survive...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Thank god... It's still here, my specimen case... They didn't take you away...

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: I guess being inconspicuous is your strength...
Verdant wipes off the ash on the glass case, eager to make sure the grass is safe.

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Verdant
steps.text: Is this.. that tuft of grass?
Lit up in the fire, Verdant beholds the sight within the case clearer than anything.
His grass can't handle the sharp rise in temperature well.
Its millet-like leaves are wilted, and its sedge-like stem is drooped. But the part that resembled bristlegrass is actually blooming.
Is that its flower? Did the fire cause the transformation? Verdant isn't sure.
No one can know for sure it is a kind of flower when they see its delicate tendrils for the first time.
The plant doesn't look like it is blooming at all with its wilted leaves and drooped stem.
But Verdant is certain that the grass is not millet, sedge, or any other kind of grass he's encountered before.
